analysis:
The supplied units are all documentation: five changelog.d entries and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. No executable source is in this batch. I found no concrete security regression and no invalidated assumption in the supplied evidence, but the changelog and doc claims describe code I could not see.

Unverified implementation contracts to check in a source pass:
- GLM-5.3-Flash is described as serving through the coordinator path with image and video input (changelog glm53-native-prerequisites.md lines 11 and 14; glm53-video-input.md line 3). That raises the surface for A-001 and TB-007: decoded-media memory caps, video decode limits, and 400 refusals.
- The GLM prefix cache is described as default-on for the pinned GLM identity (glm53-native-prerequisites.md line 9, plus DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 opt-out). This falls under T-041 and SEC-035, which cover the encrypted SSD tier and its TTFT oracle and are already accepted as open. The changelog says image and video rows never reuse cached prefixes. The doc says the complete-checkpoint store is the only GLM prefix cache. The new `key_unavailable` diagnostics and the DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE (line 21) need a check that the release build really omits that path, so no plaintext or file-based key path can reach production (T-041 mitigations).
- Local HTTP Responses continuation (local-responses-continuation.md; hardware-support.md lines 102-109) adds in-memory history. The LRU bounds the history store, but the SDK response-object store has no matching eviction. That is a memory/DoS surface on the local direct-mode server. It is local-only and the doc discloses it, so I do not treat it as a finding.
- The F_NOCACHE weight hashing (line 23) says digests are unchanged. Confirm that this does not weaken the pre-load and post-load integrity checks behind T-012 and T-027.
- New runtime capability glm5_next_v1 and hardware gating should be checked against the coordinator routing contract. That contract is outside this repo.
- Retained-fault accounting (the GLM fail-closed retirement) should be validated for availability impact, since an unproven retirement permanently holds memory until restart.

The docs-only changes do not change controls on their own.
